analysis_title: DAXDA Next-Gen Geometric & Crystallographic Synthesis: 1942 Antarctica Expeditions & Glacial Ice (Ih)
historical_clarification: In 1942, two critical Antarctic scientific records converged: (1) The February–March 1942 Argentine Antarctic Expedition aboard ARA Primero de Mayo (Deception Island & Melchior Archipelago), which executed the first Argentine Antarctic aerial photogrammetry (F-8 camera) and hydrographic/glaciological surveys; and (2) The wartime scientific compilation and NARA RG 126 archival of the U.S. Antarctic Service Expedition (USASE 1939–1941, appropriations closed 1942–1943), featuring F. Alton Wade's Ross Ice Shelf 7m pit / 41m thermohm ice-compaction dataset at West Base and Paul H. Knowles's 680-nm Palmer Peninsula geological/glaciological survey at East Base.

ice_ih_crystallography.crystal_system: Hexagonal (Disordered Proton Lattice / Pauling Residual Entropy)
ice_ih_crystallography.polyhedron_shape: Tetrahedral Oxygen Sub-lattice within Hexagonal Prism / Bipyramid Unit Cell
ice_ih_crystallography.dual_symmetry_bridge_with_fcc_metals: Ice Ih links the two primary crystallographic families in DAXDA's Planetary Metallogeny model: (1) Its macro-unit cell shares Space Group P6_3/mmc (194) and D6h (60°/120°) symmetry with Neodymium/REEs; (2) Its internal 4-coordinated oxygen hydrogen-bond network forms regular tetrahedra at 109.47°, whose supplementary dihedral angle (70.53°) is mathematically identical to the {111} octahedral slip plane angle of Face-Centered Cubic Gold (Au), Platinum (Pt), Silver (Ag), and Copper (Cu).

expedition_stations_1942.location_name: Bay of Whales, Ross Ice Shelf (Little America III)

ice_measurements.grain_size_mm: 0.5 mm (upper firn) to 3.2 mm (recrystallized shelf ice)
ice_measurements.compaction_mechanism: Mechanical settling and grain-boundary fracture compaction without meltwater recrystallization; progressive reduction of intercommunicating air channels.
